purpose: Frozen branch-only review conclusions; historical counterparts cannot set grades.

trait_findings.Coverage / protection processing: Changed-picture protection resets and short Stick/Drive timing survived retests in spring; he sustained the closest starting challenge. Two-minute, substitution and overload prompts recurred. The August mismatch was corrected, but in-season practice work and game passing are not evaluated.

strengths: Changed-picture protection resets and short Stick/Drive timing survived retests in spring; he sustained the closest starting challenge.
limitations: Two-minute, substitution and overload prompts recurred. The August mismatch was corrected, but in-season practice work and game passing are not evaluated.
Chad Henne.established: Changed-picture protection resets and on-schedule Stick/Drive timing were retained in spring. Tempo/substitution issues recurred; a full backup season gives role experience without enough game evidence for a broader ceiling.
Chad Henne.staff_view: An experienced short-game passer with enough arm to run the offense and reliable protection resets. I see his limit in hurried command and decisions once the clean rhythm breaks.

strengths: Assignment-sound spring work and cleaner final preseason operation supported QB3.
limitations: The camp menu was narrower; no regular-season passing is recorded. Full-menu changing-picture command remains untested.
John Parker Wilson.established: Assignment-sound spring work and cleaner final preseason operation supported QB3. No regular-season play is recorded. A narrower camp menu is a limit on observation, not proof that he can only run a small offense.
John Parker Wilson.staff_view: A reserve pocket quarterback whose value is clean execution of a defined menu. I would trust his preparation before I would ask him to create offense under disruption.

strengths: Cadence and feet improved, and the protection retest was correctly communicated.
limitations: Timing became late against changed presentations; the final preseason turnover and an unrecorded practice-squad season leave retention open.
Tyler Bray.established: Cadence and feet improved; protection was correctly communicated on a retest. Timing became late when the presentation changed. His practice-squad season has no recorded individual evidence.
Tyler Bray.staff_view: A developmental vertical passer with a stronger throwing tool than his command of the offense. I see a quarterback who needs timing and protection answers to catch up to the arm.

trait_findings.Pass protection: Run-track and protection communication held against changed spring and camp pictures; the season documents varied receiving work and sustained lead-back exposure. Lost fumbles require cause classification. Lower-yield runs and in-game protection lack individual evaluations; totals cannot establish decline or receiving technique.

strengths: Run-track and protection communication held against changed spring and camp pictures; the season documents varied receiving work and sustained lead-back exposure.
limitations: Lost fumbles require cause classification. Lower-yield runs and in-game protection lack individual evaluations; totals cannot establish decline or receiving technique.
Maurice Jones-Drew.established: Track and protection communication survived changed pictures in spring/camp. His season includes varied receiving work and substantial lead-back experience; recorded fumbles locate distinct review questions, not an automatic decline diagnosis.
Maurice Jones-Drew.staff_view: A compact, powerful lead back who wins with track decisions, balance and useful protection work. I see a complete veteran runner whose inside efficiency matters more than open-field speed.

trait_findings.Pass protection: Track/check responsibility held across spring looks; the correct camp scan and corrected pickup base held after teaching. The Buffalo fumble is unclassified. Contact balance was not fully tested; 17 carries and two targets cannot settle running or receiving ability.

strengths: Track/check responsibility held across spring looks; the correct camp scan and corrected pickup base held after teaching.

The back's job. Anderson reached Good in rookie minicamp, then kept the track and check responsibility in every OTA session the record covers (May 13-15, May 20-21, May 23, June 4-7) and through the June 12 changed pictures at mandatory minicamp. Stone told him that is Better in that job: retained, and correct against a changed look. In camp he found the correct scan, lost one pickup physically, corrected his base, and the correction held.
Special teams. He held a defined coverage job from camp through the season, and the two longest returns of his year, 68 at Houston and 27 at Nashville, both put the offense in the other team's half.
When his runs were called late in the year, the records show gains on the core calls: 10 on 6OL Power at Houston, 12 on Counter at Nashville.
limitations: The Buffalo fumble is unclassified. Contact balance was not fully tested; 17 carries and two targets cannot settle running or receiving ability.
Ball security. Rookie minicamp recorded Good on ball security; the Buffalo fumble reopened it. Nothing written classifies the cause, so Stone did not assign one.
Protection in games. No in-season record evaluates his protection in writing. The camp record shows one physical loss, then a correction that held; that is the last written evidence.
Contact balance. Rookie minicamp could not test it, and no later record evaluates it.
Screen and checkdown landmarks, the next step set in rookie minicamp: two targets all season. There is not enough game evidence to evaluate.
Running efficiency: 17 carries is too small a sample to say anything, and Stone said so rather than drawing a conclusion from 3.9 a carry.
C.J. Anderson.established: Track/check assignments held across spring looks; camp pickup-base correction held after teaching. The Week 15 fumble remains a cause question. Neither reserve status nor a productive run settles his full range.
C.J. Anderson.staff_view: A sturdy complementary runner with useful balance and inside finishing. I see a developing protection back, with receiving detail and open-field speed behind his inside-running tools.

strengths: Assigned receiving work held in camp and preseason; the season records finishes on Wham and Counter.

He produced when his calls came: Wham touchdowns against San Diego, Arizona and Tennessee, the Counter touchdown against Indianapolis, Draw at Kansas City, and the 28- and 39-yard catches. Four rushing touchdowns and a receiving touchdown came out of an RB2 workload.
One lost fumble all season. His assigned route work held from camp into the preseason games.
limitations: No phase supplies an individual pass-protection evaluation. The Week 14 fumble and missed targets have no written cause.

Ball security. The Week 14 fumble came at the Houston 18 in a game Jacksonville won by one point. The correction list names it; nothing written classifies the cause (carriage, contact, a second defender, the call). Stone would not guess.

Low-yield games. Denver, 10 carries for 12; Houston in Week 12, 2 for 0. The records do not say whether those runs were the blocking, the track, the read or the call, so Stone did not put them on Grimes.

Protection. No camp, preseason or in-season record contains a written evaluation of his pass protection. Stone told him he could not evaluate what nobody wrote down, and that protection and ball security are inputs the framework uses to decide how a back is used.

Receiving. Eight catches on 15 targets; the targets that were not caught are not classified, and none is charged to him. Teaching state: the preseason record supports Good on his assigned route jobs. Nothing recorded establishes Better (a correction retained against changing looks, unprompted communication), and no state was assigned for run track or protection because none was written.
Jonathan Grimes.established: Spring/preseason route assignments and backfield work provide useful positive evidence; the season gives RB2 experience. Protection and particular run/fumble causes still need individual review.
Jonathan Grimes.staff_view: A change-of-pace back with useful cuts, receiving utility and enough burst for the core runs. I see a flexible reserve, with less certainty in physical pickups and power finishing.

strengths: The record establishes a full-season fullback role with carries and receiving contributions on scoring drives.
Three of his catches after October came on touchdown drives: 34 on 22 Heavy Snag against Houston, 19 on the same call at Indianapolis, 29 at Kansas City.
No fumble in 18 games.
He dressed for every game. The Wild Card injury was cleared by the medical staff at its projection; Stone treated it as a medical fact, not a toughness finding.
limitations: Lead blocking, protection and coverage-unit technique are not individually evaluated; 15 carries do not establish short-yardage power.
Montell Owens.established: Fullback responsibilities and receiving appearances show the jobs he encountered; individual lead-block/protection execution is poorly documented. A lack of fumbles or a successful catch does not certify the whole role.
Montell Owens.staff_view: A blocking and special-teams fullback who can handle a small carry or flat-receiving package. I see utility and dependable physical work before I see a featured offensive weapon.

strengths: Assigned routes were correct in the Miami and Atlanta preseason games.
limitations: There is no individual run/protection evaluation or recorded practice-squad-season review; roster status is not a talent diagnosis.
Richard Murphy.established: Preseason Miami and Atlanta records describe assignment-correct route work. There is no documented practice-squad-season assessment, so an all-around back judgment would outrun the evidence.
Richard Murphy.staff_view: A reserve runner with usable movement and receiving assignments. I see a player who needs a specific complementary job, with protection and inside power limiting a broader role.

strengths: Practice-squad membership is established; no individual football strength can be identified from the available reps.
limitations: No named individual rep or production is recorded. Assignment, blocking and physical traits remain open without implying failure.
Will Ta'ufo'ou.established: No individual spring, preseason or practice-squad rep is recorded. The staff owes an honest evaluation; absence of a record establishes neither a physical shortfall nor a low ceiling.
Will Ta'ufo'ou.staff_view: A conventional lead-blocking fullback. My working view is that physical blocking offers his clearest role, while route versatility and receiving threaten the defense less.

trait_findings.Route running: Split/landmark corrections and formation communication transferred across spring and camp. A taught press-release correction held, and movable-H work earned an expanded receiving role. Extended press, contested-catch and drop evaluations are absent. The Divisional fumble has no classified cause; target shares are not separation grades.

strengths: Split/landmark corrections and formation communication transferred across spring and camp. A taught press-release correction held, and movable-H work earned an expanded receiving role.
limitations: Extended press, contested-catch and drop evaluations are absent. The Divisional fumble has no classified cause; target shares are not separation grades.
Adam Thielen.established: Alignment, assignment and cross-unit communication were supported in spring; recorded corrections were taken. His season brought movable receiver jobs, then an unexplained parked evaluation. One postseason fumble is a rep to understand.
Adam Thielen.staff_view: A movable possession receiver who creates value through route landmarks, hands and formation reliability. I see a developing starter whose release and vertical speed are less developed than his inside-route work.

trait_findings.Route running: Stick/Drive landmarks held against changing leverage; formation communication with Lewis and steady camp assignments supported WR1. No individual press, separation or drop findings establish the wider route profile. Intercepted targets have no receiver-responsibility classification.

strengths: Stick/Drive landmarks held against changing leverage; formation communication with Lewis and steady camp assignments supported WR1.
limitations: No individual press, separation or drop findings establish the wider route profile. Intercepted targets have no receiver-responsibility classification.
Cecil Shorts.established: Landmarks, alignment and formation communication held across spring/camp. A full season as the primary receiver gives a broad shared-QB sample; target outcomes do not by themselves establish route fault.
Cecil Shorts.staff_view: A rhythm-route receiver who can uncover on intermediate concepts and add yards after the catch. I see a legitimate starter whose route work is stronger than his contested-catch and blocking profile.

trait_findings.Coverage recognition / adjustments: Motion/split corrections held on retest; he stressed coverage when correctly aligned, and assigned routes/blocking held in the recorded Week 8 work. Alignment needed correction. Later individual blocking and receiving technique are unrecorded; suspension and game-day decisions cannot substitute for trait findings.

strengths: Motion/split corrections held on retest; he stressed coverage when correctly aligned, and assigned routes/blocking held in the recorded Week 8 work.
limitations: Alignment needed correction. Later individual blocking and receiving technique are unrecorded; suspension and game-day decisions cannot substitute for trait findings.
Justin Blackmon.established: Cumulative camp operation placed him in the leading pair; alignment/motion correction closure remains unrecorded. The later-season Z workload adds experience but cannot establish every route or blocking capability.
Justin Blackmon.staff_view: A physical outside receiver with strong hands, catch-point power and useful run-after-catch ability. I see the receiving tools ahead of the alignment and adjustment consistency needed to use them every snap.

strengths: The season records receiving contributions during the expanded role in Blackmon’s absence.
He answered when the role grew. He moved into the WR3 jobs in Week 2 with the concepts unchanged and scored in three of the next five games.
Late in the year Mesh found him, and each of those four catches came on a scoring drive, two of them in the playoffs. The Cleveland touchdown put Jacksonville ahead in a game it won in overtime.
Returns: eight kickoffs by situation. Stone did not grade them in the meeting; the return evaluation is a special-teams follow-up (Stone until the coordinator job is filled).
limitations: Individual route work is thin. The Week 4 fumble was coached but its cause is unrecorded; randomly attributed returns do not certify return skill.

Ball security after the catch. The Indianapolis fumble is the only one in his record; it was coached on the Monday film and did not recur. Stone classified it as a football mistake: coached and re-checked, not punished.

The practice record is thin. No spring phase record names him, and camp recorded him as depth. Stone told him the staff cannot state a Good, Better or Best reading for him from the written record, and would not invent one. His 2014 evaluation needs practice evidence, not only game results.
Two short catches lost yardage (Weeks 5 and 10). Nothing written classifies them, and Stone drew no conclusion from them.
Toney Clemons.established: He transferred into the WR3 job with the concept structure intact. Individual practice detail is thin; the Week 4 fumble and target outcomes need context. Old randomly allocated return credits do not assess him.
Toney Clemons.staff_view: A reserve outside receiver with more vertical utility than polished route detail. I see situational depth who needs cleaner adjustments and dependable catch execution to claim a larger job.

strengths: The recorded reserve contribution includes five catches on five targets against San Diego and a 22-yard Seattle catch.
limitations: Spring/camp individual technique and defensive response are not evaluated. Inactive status was a numbers decision, not a recorded football flaw.
Mike Brown.established: San Diego supplies representative receiving opportunities, including Split Leak; practice assessment is thin. Week 11 inactivity followed roster composition changes and is not recorded as a finding against his play.
Mike Brown.staff_view: A short-area reserve receiver who can work underneath routes and offer modest run-after-catch utility. I see depth rather than a receiver I would feature against press or at the catch point.

strengths: Practice-squad membership is established; the record does not support naming a specific receiving strength.
limitations: No named individual rep or season statistic supplies route, hands or speed evidence. Missing evaluation does not imply low ability.
Jerrell Jackson.established: No individual 2013 rep or practice-squad evaluation is recorded. He asked for written feedback; the missing communication belongs to the staff before any conclusion about his football ability.
Jerrell Jackson.staff_view: A developmental receiver with useful movement but an unfinished NFL route and adjustment profile. I see a practice-squad receiver competing for a narrow depth role.

trait_findings.Alignment versatility: Formation communication transferred through minicamp; camp described the most dependable all-around tight-end operator, and assigned preseason routes held. Individual run-block and protection findings are not recorded. Delay calls and team rushing totals cannot identify his block quality.

strengths: Formation communication transferred through minicamp; camp described the most dependable all-around tight-end operator, and assigned preseason routes held.
limitations: Individual run-block and protection findings are not recorded. Delay calls and team rushing totals cannot identify his block quality.
Marcedes Lewis.established: Formation communication, dependable all-around camp operation and assignment-correct preseason routes are supported. Extensive protection assignments make low receiving totals an incomplete picture; in-line execution still needs his own review.
Marcedes Lewis.staff_view: A large, complete attached tight end whose blocking, catch radius and dependable operation anchor the position. I see a strong starter who offers more structure and physical usefulness than sudden separation.

trait_findings.Alignment versatility: Alignment and assigned receiving responsibilities held in camp/preseason; he retained TE3/13-personnel availability. Blocking, protection and coverage-unit technique are not evaluated. Two regular-season targets are insufficient for a receiving trait benchmark.

strengths: Alignment and assigned receiving responsibilities held in camp/preseason; he retained TE3/13-personnel availability.

Assignment reliability on routes. Camp and two preseason games record the same thing: he ran the route he was given. That meets the assignment part of the Good description (knows where to line up, knows his assignment), and Stone told him so; the record holds nothing on his communication or technique, so Stone took the reading no further.
Availability. He dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both playoff games, and held the 13-personnel job the weekly records assign him.
limitations: Blocking, protection and coverage-unit technique are not evaluated. Two regular-season targets are insufficient for a receiving trait benchmark.
Allen Reisner.established: Camp/preseason assignment reliability and route work provide a baseline. TE3 usage leaves individual blocking and broader receiving capability underobserved, not disproven.
Allen Reisner.staff_view: An assignment-oriented third tight end suited to attached and heavy-personnel work. I see a dependable package player with limited receiving separation and little reason to feature him in space.

trait_findings.Run blocking: Attached/wing-to-flex alignment corrections held through spring; moving routes earned second-group work and transferred to preseason assignments. Run-block base, hands and pad level needed repeated correction after alignment changes. These are recorded technique losses, with no in-game blocking retest.

strengths: Attached/wing-to-flex alignment corrections held through spring; moving routes earned second-group work and transferred to preseason assignments.

Alignment and assignment. Rookie minicamp recorded Good on the attached/wing alignment menu. In OTAs he "handled attached-to-flex alignment changes correctly," and the standouts record reads "Alignment knowledge traveled." No phase record shows an assignment error; every recorded correction was technique.

Route and movement work that transferred. Camp: "Kelce's best movement/route work earned a defined second-group role." Preseason: held his route assignment on a touchdown drive against the Jets; transferred his assigned route job against Philadelphia; sustained it at Atlanta. He carried three weeks of in-season additions and was in the regular call structure from Week 8.
His four catches from Week 10 through the Wild Card went for 36 at Tennessee, 14 against Buffalo, 28 against Tennessee and 53 at Kansas City.
limitations: Run-block base, hands and pad level needed repeated correction after alignment changes. These are recorded technique losses, with no in-game blocking retest.
Travis Kelce.established: Attached/flex alignment and route movement transferred across spring, preseason and the assigned season role. Base/hand work in attached blocking required repeated teaching; assignment understanding and physical execution must stay separate.
Travis Kelce.staff_view: A receiving tight end who can move between attached, wing and flex alignments. I see movement and route potential in his current tools, with blocking leverage and hands still behind his receiving work.

trait_findings.Recovery / balance: The preseason Atlanta record identifies a correct protection responsibility and recovery after leverage loss. Individual camp/game blocking findings are sparse. Randomly assigned sacks cannot support an elite pass-protection grade; unit exchanges are not his individual evidence.

strengths: The preseason Atlanta record identifies a correct protection responsibility and recovery after leverage loss.
limitations: Individual camp/game blocking findings are sparse. Randomly assigned sacks cannot support an elite pass-protection grade; unit exchanges are not his individual evidence.
Eugene Monroe.established: A full season of tackle responsibility supplies experience and review material. The individual record supports some correctly identified work with physical-leverage questions, not a complete grade from sacks charged by the old engine.
Eugene Monroe.staff_view: A balanced starting left tackle with useful pass-set movement, recovery and sufficient anchor. I see pass protection as his best contribution, with solid rather than dominant drive blocking.

trait_findings.Twist / blitz recognition: Hand and twist-spacing corrections held through changed fronts; set/run assignments and combination communication with Rackley transferred across camp. Occasional leverage loss is a technique question. Charged sacks are random assignments; chip/help plans alone do not establish an individual weakness.

strengths: Hand and twist-spacing corrections held through changed fronts; set/run assignments and combination communication with Rackley transferred across camp.
limitations: Occasional leverage loss is a technique question. Charged sacks are random assignments; chip/help plans alone do not establish an individual weakness.
Lane Johnson.established: Point echoes, changed-front communication and twist exchanges were retained through spring/camp. The rookie then started a full season. Physical answers to power/inside counters remain a question, distinct from understanding.
Lane Johnson.staff_view: An athletic starting right tackle who can move on reach and second-level work and retain taught protection answers. I see leverage, hand precision and consistent anchoring as the remaining limits of his rookie profile.

trait_findings.Recovery / balance: Camp recorded recovery and rush pickup after leverage loss; subsequent practice supported the primary interior-reserve role. Combination communication was less consistent than Rackley’s in the compared camp work. Dressing does not establish snaps or a full blocking evaluation.

strengths: Camp recorded recovery and rush pickup after leverage loss; subsequent practice supported the primary interior-reserve role.
Recovery and rush pickup, the two individual positives camp recorded, and what kept the competition live.

Assignment identification: Preseason Game 1. Preseason protection notes came in part from automated sack attribution (Preseason Game 3 record), so this one is read alongside the camp record, not alone.
limitations: Combination communication was less consistent than Rackley’s in the compared camp work. Dressing does not establish snaps or a full blocking evaluation.
Combination communication. Camp separated the two guards on Rackley's communication holding late in practice. That is communication, not a physical finding.
Initial leverage: lost before recovering in camp and in Preseason Game 1. Technique, not effort.

Stone was plain that the in-season record is thin: one bye practice, then eight regular-season and two playoff games dressed as reserve with no individual evaluation recorded. Teaching state: Good (assignment identified, a live competitor through camp). Better, which asks for unprompted communication and technique reproduced through changing looks, is not established: combination communication was the part camp called less consistent, and the season added no individual evidence.
Austin Pasztor.established: Identification and interior communication have supporting camp evidence; isolated recovery after losing leverage was less settled. Missing weeks caused by the injury-record problem are not an effort or learning finding.
Austin Pasztor.staff_view: A physical interior reserve with useful recovery but uneven combinations and leverage. I see a backup who can cover a job, with less consistent coordination than the starting pair.

trait_findings.Protection identification / calls: Protection-point declarations, self-correction and teaching helped the interior group operate against changing fronts with less coach rescue. Physical combination work needed pads; there is no later individual camp/game blocking assessment. Injury and the starter change are not ability grades.

strengths: Protection-point declarations, self-correction and teaching helped the interior group operate against changing fronts with less coach rescue.
Communication. Point declaration, fewer coach-dependent corrections, the point-echo-confirmation reduction built with Tice, and changed-front and twist work finished without rescue.
Readiness after clearance: ready as reserve every week ("Brad dresses and he's one snap from playing").
limitations: Physical combination work needed pads; there is no later individual camp/game blocking assessment. Injury and the starter change are not ability grades.
Physical combinations: spring left them for padded work, and camp recorded only that he continued to stabilize the line. No individual physical finding exists, and Stone did not invent one.

Stone told him the center job moved on Brewster's execution while Meester was injured, not on a finding against Meester. Teaching state: for the spring phases, the communication record fits the framework's Best description (self-corrects routine problems, helps the man next to him without losing his own job). That state covers communication only: the technique half was left for padded work, and camp gave no individual finding on it. No in-season state can be given after Week 2; the record holds none.
Brad Meester.established: Communication and point/echo/confirm work provide a recorded veteran contribution. His two starts and reserve period deserve the promised review. Entry 79 retirement ends training eligibility.
Brad Meester.staff_view: A veteran center whose protection calls and communication remain his defining value. I see a player who can organize a line, with movement and sustained physical blocking below his mental operation.

trait_findings.Pass-set / mirror: Assignment responses held in padded camp; preseason protection identification was correct. Leverage was lost despite correct identification. Six-lineman rushing outcomes are collective; individual game snap and technique evidence are absent.

strengths: Assignment responses held in padded camp; preseason protection identification was correct.

Assignment. The first padded camp work records "a sound response," and Preseason Game 1 has him identifying his protection job. That meets the Good description at camp and preseason contact level, and Stone told him so.

Two jobs held through the season: swing tackle, and sixth lineman from Week 5 through the Divisional plan. Under the program's rule a poor package can shrink or disappear, and the 6OL package kept its place. Stone said the record does not separate his share of that from the other ten players', and did not hand him the yards.
limitations: Leverage was lost despite correct identification. Six-lineman rushing outcomes are collective; individual game snap and technique evidence are absent.

Leverage after a correct identification. The one technique note (Miami) records that he lost leverage physically after identifying his protection job, and continued the rep. There is no effort finding.

The record itself. Nothing written evaluates his 6OL snaps or any tackle work after camp. Stone said the evaluation would be no thicker than that until Yarno's film sort exists. Teaching state: Good on assignment in camp and preseason. Nothing in the record shows Better either way.
Cameron Bradfield.established: Correct identification with physical-leverage loss and recovery appears in preseason. Swing/six-lineman usage provides experience; it does not certify every tackle job or explain every team run result.
Cameron Bradfield.staff_view: A swing tackle and heavy-package blocker who can recognize the job and cover either edge in a reserve role. I see assignment utility ahead of his recovery ceiling against NFL rushers.

trait_findings.Snap / operation: He held the center operation while Meester was injured and retained the full starter job after the first three games of that exposure. Starter selection is not proof of every call or snap. Preseason leverage/recovery notes require film attribution; individual game center grades are absent.

strengths: He held the center operation while Meester was injured and retained the full starter job after the first three games of that exposure.

He took over the whole center job in one week and the operation held. Stone's caution from Seattle stands ("Zero sacks is the line and everyone on it, not just him"); the individual evidence is Stone's sequence of decisions: continuity, then execution, confirmed on three games, kept at the bye. Nothing in the record reversed it.

Identification: the one individual technique note, from August, records the assignment identified correctly and recovery after the loss. That note is tied to the game's one sack, and preseason protection notes came in part from automated attribution (Preseason Game 3 record), so it is read only alongside center week and the in-season decisions, not alone.
limitations: Starter selection is not proof of every call or snap. Preseason leverage/recovery notes require film attribution; individual game center grades are absent.

Leverage after a correct identification: the Preseason Game 2 rep (with the caveat above), the pattern camp recorded for the whole protection unit ("Assignments were generally identified; leverage and physical finish produced sacks"). Technique, not assignment or effort.

Stone was plain that the in-season record on him is thin. After Seattle he said publicly he would "grade the calls on tape"; no grade is recorded, and the bye record reports the sort of sacks by cause only for the group. He did not substitute a verdict from memory. Teaching state: Good, on the recorded decisions (he knew the job, communicated it and held it at game speed). Better, which asks for retained corrections and unprompted communication across changing looks, is not established: no individual grade of his calls exists.
Mike Brewster.established: He took over the center role during the season and the recorded operation held. Individual season grades were not returned; the protection unit's outcomes cannot establish all of his physical execution.
Mike Brewster.staff_view: A young center who can hold the operation and communicate the core protection work. I see a viable starting option whose anchor, leverage and second-level work remain less developed than his operation.

trait_findings.Interior pass protection: The preseason record identifies assigned protection correctly; interior communication was corrected within the group. Leverage loss followed correct identification. Group self-correction cannot all be credited to him, and later individual findings are missing.

strengths: The preseason record identifies assigned protection correctly; interior communication was corrected within the group.
Availability: he dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both postseason games and held the left-guard job in each.

Assignment and communication. Miami has him identifying the protection job. The OTA interior transfer was late once and then corrected by the line without a coach. Stone said that exchange, a unit correction he was part of, shows one part of the Better description, communicating without prompting; the record credits the line, not him alone, and does not show the correction retained.
limitations: Leverage loss followed correct identification. Group self-correction cannot all be credited to him, and later individual findings are missing.
Leverage after a correct identification. Miami records that he lost leverage physically after identifying the job, and continued the rep; there is no effort finding.

The in-season record is thin. After Week 3 he appears only in line listings, and the one individual item, the Oakland sack, was reviewed before Seattle and sorted with every other sack at the bye, but no result for it is written down. Stone said that is a gap in the staff's work, not a finding about him. Teaching state: Good on assignment and communication in spring and preseason; one part of Better (communication without prompting) shown by the line, not by him individually, on the OTA interior exchange. No in-season record supports a state either way.
Uche Nwaneri.established: Correct identification and recovery appear in preseason; shared interior exchange work improved in spring. Individual leverage and the Week 2 sack cause remain underclassified. A VERIFY retirement row does not retire him.
Uche Nwaneri.staff_view: A power-oriented starting guard with useful interior anchor and drive blocking. I see less advantage on movement work and a need for steadier leverage after correctly identifying the assignment.

trait_findings.Combination / second-level work: Stable late-camp combination communication held on repeated calls and supported the right-guard decision. Occasional leverage loss/recovery remains a technique question. Medical limitations and randomly assigned sacks cannot diagnose blocking ability.

strengths: Stable late-camp combination communication held on repeated calls and supported the right-guard decision.

Communication. It is what won him the job: the more consistent combination calls in the first pads, communication that "held late in practice," and the best cumulative first-unit communication in camp. That meets Good, and points to the communication part of Better.

Availability: he dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both postseason games. He carried a limited listing from Week 4 on (minor trunk in Week 4, minor upper extremity from Week 5); Stone said that is a medical fact and not a toughness or effort finding in either direction.
limitations: Occasional leverage loss/recovery remains a technique question. Medical limitations and randomly assigned sacks cannot diagnose blocking ability.

Recovery after losing initial leverage. Camp gave Pasztor the better isolated recovery, Miami recorded a leverage loss, and the standouts entry keeps "occasional leverage losses" as technique work. That is the recorded target, and it is the technique part of Better that the record does not yet show.

The in-season record is thin: line listings, charged sacks and availability. Stone said his evaluation stops there until Yarno's sort exists, and that the sort will not read any rep as caused by the limitation without the medical staff. Teaching state: Good, with the communication part of Better supported; the technique part of Better (reproducing technique through repeated reps) is not yet shown.
Will Rackley.established: Combination calls were consistent late in camp and supported the starting decision. Physical recovery/leverage was less settled. Injury-limited opportunity cannot be interpreted as toughness, effort or stalled learning.
Will Rackley.staff_view: A combination-oriented guard whose communication can support a coherent starting unit. I see functional inside strength, with individual leverage and recovery limiting a higher grade.

strengths: The record establishes six game-day appearances as interior reserve, without an identifiable individual football strength.
limitations: No spring, camp or preseason record names an individual rep or measured snap. The reserve-slot change rested on Pasztor’s work, not a recorded Asper correction.
Mark Asper.established: The individual record is too thin to establish technique strengths or faults; charged sacks do not prove he even participated. The reserve-order change cited Pasztor's work, not an Asper failure.
Mark Asper.staff_view: An interior depth lineman whose clearest route to a role is size and basic power work. My view is that protection coordination, movement and recovery need a defined backup assignment.

trait_findings.Gap discipline / lateral pursuit: The Marks/Miller pair supplied the most stable recorded interior camp fit; the front call arrived early in the scrimmage. Individual get-off, hands, anchor and rush counters are not classified. Depth-based tackles/sacks/pressures and unit run losses cannot grade those traits.

strengths: The Marks/Miller pair supplied the most stable recorded interior camp fit; the front call arrived early in the scrimmage.
limitations: Individual get-off, hands, anchor and rush counters are not classified. Depth-based tackles/sacks/pressures and unit run losses cannot grade those traits.
Sen'Derrick Marks.established: Camp identified a stable interior run combination with Miller. His season contains different rush/contain purposes; sack and pressure counts cannot tell whether he followed those purposes.
Sen'Derrick Marks.staff_view: A penetrating interior starter whose quick entry and lateral pursuit can disrupt the pocket and backfield. I see better single-gap pressure tools than double-team anchoring.

strengths: The first padded-camp block supported retention in the edge rotation.
Camp. He held his place in the edge/strong-side rotation through the first physical work.
Availability. Dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both playoff games with no receipt injury; third in every recorded edge order from Week 2 through Week 8.
Week 4, the one week an edge row's evidence column names him: "Babin and Branch two tackles each."
limitations: No later individual edge technique or game exposure is evaluated. Four tackles and zero sacks are not evidence of failed pass-rush ability.
Nothing written supports a technique finding, good or bad, and Stone would not invent one. The questions for his film are the room's: containment on the directive weeks, rush lanes, and finish.

What he will be judged on in 2014 is the edge job as the program writes it: an edge knows "when they are responsible for the quarterback, the back, boot action or contain," and the Good, Better, Best descriptions of assignment, correction retention and changing looks. Teaching state: none recorded. Stone did not assign one.
Andre Branch.established: Camp established edge/strong-side rotation experience; the player reported that paired teaching helped. Individual season rush/run execution is not yet fully classified.
Andre Branch.staff_view: A rotational edge defender with useful first-step and pursuit tools. I see a rusher who needs a more developed hand/counter plan and firmer edge work to become a dependable full-time starter.

strengths: Camp established an edge/strong-side rotation role before his long injury absence.
limitations: Only two games were active and no individual technique correction is documented. The injury is a medical limitation, not a grade; the historical DE must not be confused with the same-name corner.
C.J. Wilson.established: Recorded camp edge/strong-side work provides limited baseline evidence. A prolonged absence left individual evaluation thin; historical medical gaps are not ability conclusions.
C.J. Wilson.staff_view: A strong-side edge defender whose power and run setting offer more than bend or speed. I see a rotational run defender with limited reason to feature him as a wide speed rusher.

strengths: Camp identified him as the leading edge-pressure option in the current rotation.
The camp rush. "Leading edge-rush pressure" in the first physical work, the edge work before Miami, and the edge job at camp close.
Week 14. His first-half sack forced the punt before the 80-yard touchdown drive in the 21-20 win over Houston, and he had two sacks that night. Week 15, the only sack of Manuel.
Availability. Dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both playoff games, first in every recorded edge order, no receipt injury.

Quarterback containment in the late directive weeks held: Manuel, Locker (Week 16) and Luck ran for 4, 10 and 2 yards. The edge rows also record "Rush lanes held" (Week 3) and "Contained" (Weeks 6 and 7). Stone called these unit results and did not credit them to Babin individually.
limitations: A particular rush move, finish and contain responsibility are not individually classified. Role-derived counts and unit containment reads cannot fill that gap.

Finish. Pressures are credited in Weeks 2 to 4, then none until Week 14, and none in Weeks 16 and 17 or the playoffs; no sack through Week 13. Stone set out the whole picture first: the contain directives begin in Week 8, Weeks 5 to 7 carry neither a directive nor a credited pressure, and the Week 6 plan already recorded 2 sacks in five games. He called it a film question, not a verdict.

Contain. Kaepernick's 30-yard run (Week 8), Schaub's 9 and 10 (Week 14) and Locker's 13-yard scramble on the Divisional go-ahead drive. None of those records names an edge, and none goes in his column before the film is sorted. Teaching state: Stone told him the camp rush meets Good as a rusher at camp contact level. He did not name Better, because nothing written records his corrections or how he handled changed looks.
Jason Babin.established: Camp identified leading edge pressure. The season requires separating called containment from chances to finish; raw sack totals cannot provide that split.
Jason Babin.staff_view: A pass-rush-oriented edge veteran with get-off, bend and a useful rush plan. I see pressure value above his point-of-attack and containment contribution.

strengths: The record includes a London sack and a Houston run-loss outcome in the second edge role.

London. Ahead 20-13, right after the interception at 3:27, his sack of Kaepernick came on the possession that ended in a San Francisco punt. Stone said that is the first rep he would put in any cutup of the season.
Houston away. The 10-yard loss on Foster on Houston's first series was part of the stop that produced a punt from the Houston 16, in a game Jacksonville lost 38-6.
Availability. Dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both playoff games, second in every recorded edge order, no receipt injury.
limitations: No spring/camp individual technique evaluation identifies the cause of those outcomes. Unit containment questions are not assigned to him.

The record. A 16-game starter in 2012, he is not named in any 2013 spring, camp or preseason record, and the week files describe two of his plays. Stone told him plainly that he could not give him a teaching state from that, and would not invent a flaw to fill the gap.

The room's open questions apply to him as much as anyone: finish (the bye correction) and containment on the directive weeks (Kaepernick's 30-yard run in Week 8, Schaub's scrambles of 9 and 10 in Week 14, Locker's 13-yard scramble in the Divisional game). None of those records names an edge; all of them wait for the film. Teaching state: none recorded. Stone did not assign one.
Jeremy Mincey.established: The role history includes an edge rotation, but no sufficient individual spring/camp evaluation identifies why he ranked there. It is not a complete description of his capacity.
Jeremy Mincey.staff_view: A sturdy edge defender who offers power, run setting and rotational rush work. I see a balanced role player whose speed/bend are less threatening than his physical edge play.

trait_findings.Gap discipline / lateral pursuit: Camp established a stable starting interior pairing and a run-priority role alongside Marks. Individual anchor, double-team and fit classifications are absent. A low sack total in a run-priority role does not establish a pass-rush ceiling.

strengths: Camp established a stable starting interior pairing and a run-priority role alongside Marks.

The job he was signed for. The interior run fit held in camp. In the season the weekly records list the run defense as holding in Weeks 1, 4, 7, 8, 11, 14, 16 and 17 and the Wild Card; those are unit results, like the corrections. The Week 16 rematch answered Week 10: his seven tackles in a game Tennessee ran 20 times for 77 yards.
Available every week, and the Week 10 safety.
limitations: Individual anchor, double-team and fit classifications are absent. A low sack total in a run-priority role does not establish a pass-rush ceiling.

The run games that went wrong (Week 10's fourth quarter, Weeks 12, 13 and 15, the Divisional) are recorded against the unit. His reps inside them are classified by the state/05 categories before any fault is his; Stone assumed none.

The rush line (1 sack, 7 pressures) cannot be read yet. Several weekly directives put the run fit first ("fit Richardson before rushing past the run," "Johnson's run fit before the rush plan"), and the staff holds no classified rush reps for him. Teaching state: for camp, his base run fit meets the Good description (he knew and executed the fit at the contact level camp allowed, in the most stable pairing). Nothing recorded individually reaches Better, and nothing recorded says he fell short of it.
Roy Miller.established: Base-front fit was supported in camp, including the interior pairing with Marks. A run-first assignment can suppress rush opportunities; individual game evidence still needs classification.
Roy Miller.staff_view: A run-priority interior anchor built to occupy blocks and hold the front. I see his double-team and power work ahead of penetration and developed pass-rush counters.

strengths: Camp established rotation versatility across the front; the season records three sacks.

Finishing when the play came to him: the Week 7 sack, the two-sack Arizona game, and three tackles for loss, two of them in the Week 14 win over Houston, where he was one of the three players who stopped three straight Houston runs for losses.
Carrying a job across the front. Camp recorded him "rotating across the front," and he held that job, available, every week.
limitations: The record does not classify individual get-off, fit or counters. The starting-pair decision and sack counts do not identify a technical weakness.

The starting order was a comparison, not a finding against him. Camp named Miller and Marks the most stable run combination; no record names a lost fit, a missed assignment or a technique fault of his. Stone told him that plainly and did not invent one.

His individual evidence is missing: none of his reps is classified in any record. A blank line in a rotation game is not read as a flaw, and his reps inside the corrections of Weeks 10, 12, 13 and 15 and the Divisional are classified by the state/05 categories before anything is assigned to him. Teaching state: the record gives no individual phase state, and Stone did not build one from box-score lines.
Tyson Alualu.established: Experience across front jobs is recorded, but the individual physical/technical evaluation is thin. A stronger camp pairing elsewhere does not identify his defect or settle his best job.
Tyson Alualu.staff_view: A versatile rotational front player who can handle several alignments and supply useful power. I see positional flexibility before I see a defining rush counter or disruptive specialty.

strengths: Preseason finishes supported earning the fourth edge-rotation job.
limitations: No comparable in-season snap or individual rush assessment is recorded. One assist and zero sacks do not show that the preseason skill disappeared.
Ryan Davis.established: Camp/preseason rush finishes earned rotational work. The season does not record his rush opportunity denominator, so low production cannot distinguish limited opportunity from execution.
Ryan Davis.staff_view: A developmental rotational rusher with a useful first step. I see a situational pressure option whose edge anchor and block defeat need to catch up to his movement tools.

trait_findings.Contain discipline: Rookie work correctly communicated base edge/contain responsibility; a widened rush-lane landmark was corrected on repeat. The initial lane error was technical. Later individual reps and game exposure are not evaluated, so retained containment over a full season remains open.

strengths: Rookie work correctly communicated base edge/contain responsibility; a widened rush-lane landmark was corrected on repeat.
limitations: The initial lane error was technical. Later individual reps and game exposure are not evaluated, so retained containment over a full season remains open.
Lavar Edwards.established: Rookie minicamp recorded known edge/contain assignments and an immediate rush-lane correction. Later individual evidence is thin despite dressing late in the year.
Lavar Edwards.staff_view: A developmental edge player with enough power and assignment understanding for a narrow package. I see his lane discipline and hand work as the steps between rookie depth and a stable rotation job.

strengths: The record establishes late-season interior rotation exposure, including recorded tackles and a sack.
limitations: There is no classified individual rep. The prolonged injury-status projection was a record problem, not football failure; this is the veteran DT, not the later LB.
C.J. Mosley.established: His long early absence was prolonged by the club's record failure. Later interior rotation supplies review material, but there is no sound individual ability conclusion from counts alone.
C.J. Mosley.staff_view: A veteran interior reserve who can supply strength and hold a limited run assignment. I see more value in occupying a block than in creating repeated penetration or rush-counter wins.

strengths: Seven game-day appearances establish interior-reserve availability.
limitations: No named camp technique or individual snap evaluation is recorded. Later inactivity followed a numbers decision; a single tackle cannot rank ability.
Jeris Pendleton.established: Seven dressed games have no individual written evaluation; later inactivity was a game-day-list choice. Neither physical shortfall nor effort failure is established.
Jeris Pendleton.staff_view: A power-oriented interior reserve. I see a narrow run-defense role, with first-step disruption, hand technique and pass-rush development below his raw strength.

strengths: Practice-squad membership is established; a specific individual line strength is not documented.
limitations: There is no named rep or season production. Size, roster status and missing evaluations cannot manufacture an anchor or rush weakness.
Jerome Long.established: No individual 2013 rep or practice-squad evaluation is recorded. His question about weight does not establish that weight is the problem.
Jerome Long.staff_view: A developmental interior lineman who offers size and a basic power role. My working view is that block defeat and disciplined technique are the larger questions than raw strength.

strengths: Practice-squad membership and prior experience are established, without a new individual trait finding.
limitations: No named 2013 rep or individual season evaluation is recorded. Prior experience and practice-squad status cannot establish current physical or technical standing.
D'Anthony Smith.established: Prior NFL experience is recorded, but this staff's 2013 individual evidence is missing. A vacant roster place does not establish why he was not promoted.
D'Anthony Smith.staff_view: A developmental interior defender with some initial movement utility. I see a player who needs stronger anchoring and a defined hand/counter sequence to earn a regular rotation job.

trait_findings.Communication: Spring/camp second-level communication stabilized; he retained the base communication lead from Week 4 through the postseason despite role changes. Individual keys, drops and run fits are not classified in the season. Opponent tight-end targets and role-derived tackles cannot assign coverage responsibility.

strengths: Spring/camp second-level communication stabilized; he retained the base communication lead from Week 4 through the postseason despite role changes.
limitations: Individual keys, drops and run fits are not classified in the season. Opponent tight-end targets and role-derived tackles cannot assign coverage responsibility.
Daryl Smith.established: Dated branch records support communication when Posluszny was absent, including the reshaped late-season base. Tight-end targets and run outcomes require assignment/help review before individual judgment.
Daryl Smith.staff_view: A complete second-level veteran whose communication, diagnosis and zone awareness organize the defense. I see a strong starter whose value is reading and coordinating rather than being a featured pressure player.

trait_findings.Communication: Front-fit calls stabilized the spring group with less coach rescue and helped others finish without repeated confirmation. Later individual run keys, fit and coverage evaluations are absent. Medical restrictions and delegated communication do not imply a talent decline.

strengths: Front-fit calls stabilized the spring group with less coach rescue and helped others finish without repeated confirmation.
limitations: Later individual run keys, fit and coverage evaluations are absent. Medical restrictions and delegated communication do not imply a talent decline.
Paul Posluszny.established: A season of fits/calls and an explicit request to clarify shared command belong in his profile. Much in-season evidence is unit-level; the independent medical hold limits current work, not his standing as a learner.
Paul Posluszny.staff_view: An instinctive middle linebacker who can set fits, communicate the front and finish inside tackles. I see downhill work as stronger than isolated man coverage or recovery range.

trait_findings.Communication: Coverage-lane communication retained teaching in camp; the record documents preparation and retention when his defensive role expanded. Special-teams learning cannot automatically grade base defensive fits. Individual in-game run and coverage responsibilities are not classified.

strengths: Coverage-lane communication retained teaching in camp; the record documents preparation and retention when his defensive role expanded.

Ready when the job moved. His role changed on a week's notice twice, in Week 4 and Week 14. Week 4's record says the linebacker operation held, and Week 14's lists "Smith and Allen in the reshaped base defense" as held up. Stone repeated his own Week 15 note to him: correctly done.

Finishing the plays that came to him: the Arizona interception that became three points before the half, the Wild Card interception that set up the first touchdown, and the Week 13 sack on Cleveland's first series.

Coverage units. Camp recorded repeated, communicated lane execution and finish. By the framework's definitions, reproducing a communicated job through repeated reps is Better. Stone said that is the one teaching state the record supports for him, and only for that job in that phase.
limitations: Special-teams learning cannot automatically grade base defensive fits. Individual in-game run and coverage responsibilities are not classified.

Run fits in his starts. By unit result they held in Weeks 14, 16 and 17 and the Wild Card, and were corrected in Week 15 and the Divisional. Neither correction has been classified by cause, so nothing in them is assigned to him until the review says whose fit broke and why (assignment, communication, technique, physical loss, processing, or the call).
Linebacker evidence is otherwise unit reads and tackle totals. Stone did not build a linebacker teaching state from box-score lines and said so.
Russell Allen.established: Branch records describe ready operation beside Smith during teammate absences and retained narrow coverage/communication work. His full individual fit/coverage review remains owed.
Russell Allen.staff_view: A dependable complementary linebacker and coverage-unit contributor who can prepare for expanded assignments. I see a role player with communication value and less ability to dictate pressure or man-matchups.

trait_findings.Fit discipline: Pursuit/change-of-direction work and taught coverage landmarks/handoffs transferred against changed spring distributions. A run-fit overrun corrected in camp recurred in the scrimmage and narrowed the package. No later individual package retest establishes full closure.

strengths: Pursuit/change-of-direction work and taught coverage landmarks/handoffs transferred against changed spring distributions.

Corrections held. Every spring correction the record names for him (the rookie-minicamp landmark, the OTA coverage landmark, the changed-distribution handoff) held on the retest. Rookie minicamp recorded Good. By the framework's definitions, retaining corrections and executing against changing looks is Better, and that is what the OTA and minicamp record describes on those coverage jobs. The record does not use the word; Stone said so.
Speed that shows up in the right places: "Pursuit movement and space change-of-direction" at rookie minicamp, "pressure and pursuit were useful" at the scrimmage.
Available every week of his first season.
limitations: A run-fit overrun corrected in camp recurred in the scrimmage and narrowed the package. No later individual package retest establishes full closure.

Fit discipline at full speed. He overran a fit in camp, took the correction, then overran one again at the scrimmage, and Crennel narrowed his assignment. Bush's camp correction was a leverage correction, which points to technique at speed rather than assignment; the scrimmage overrun itself is not classified in the record, and Stone said so. Stone's reading on that job was Good, not yet Better: the correction held once and the overrun came back once.
The season itself is unclassified. Stone would not put a teaching state on sixteen games of package work that no record breaks down.
Sio Moore.established: Spring coverage correction held under changed looks, with useful movement/pursuit evidence. Camp fit overruns recurred after an earlier correction, narrowing the assigned job at that time.
Sio Moore.staff_view: An athletic package linebacker with range and useful pressure tools. I see his movement ahead of his run diagnosis and fit consistency, which need to become dependable before expanding the job.

strengths: The season establishes first base-reserve availability and an expanded role in Week 14.
limitations: No individual practice or game classification supplies a run-fit, tackling or coverage grade. Recorded tackles do not supply that finding.
Julian Stanford.established: Late-season base-reserve responsibility provides meaningful exposure but no completed fit-by-fit assessment. Tackles locate involvement rather than prove the fit was right.
Julian Stanford.staff_view: A mobile reserve linebacker who can cover space and take a defined replacement assignment. I see limited block destruction and coverage detail as the barriers to a larger base role.

trait_findings.Zone / pattern match: Camp/scrimmage documented sound leverage exchanges and technical work during controlled return to full participation. No individual target responsibility or current recovery-speed test is recorded. Unit coverage results cannot rank technique, and old workouts cannot certify post-injury speed.

strengths: Camp/scrimmage documented sound leverage exchanges and technical work during controlled return to full participation.
limitations: No individual target responsibility or current recovery-speed test is recorded. Unit coverage results cannot rank technique, and old workouts cannot certify post-injury speed.
Brent Grimes.established: Camp supports sound leverage and clear exchanges. The full season raises meaningful help/target questions, but totals cannot reconstruct individual responsibility.
Brent Grimes.staff_view: A technically sharp coverage corner with excellent short-area reactions, eyes and ball play. I see off coverage and pattern recognition as his strengths, with size/power and block defeat less favorable.

trait_findings.Zone / pattern match: Comparable camp outside work supported the starting job; preseason coverage communication and pursuit were recorded positively. Later target/technique responsibility is not classified. Injury and aggregate unit results cannot establish an individual coverage weakness.

strengths: Comparable camp outside work supported the starting job; preseason coverage communication and pursuit were recorded positively.
He won the job the contract only let him compete for, held it from the second camp block through camp close, and started every game until he was hurt.
The Week 1 interception that became a touchdown drive; the Seattle game in a three-point road win; and four straight weeks (5 to 8) of positive reads for the outside pair.
Teams portability, which the contract named: preseason Game 4.
limitations: Later target/technique responsibility is not classified. Injury and aggregate unit results cannot establish an individual coverage weakness.
None the record can name. No record assigns him a coverage loss, missed tackle or technique fault, and Stone did not invent one.

His reps inside the unit corrections (Seattle's last possession, Cook, the Mathews touchdown) are classified by the state/05 categories before anything is assigned to him. Teaching state: the record holds a camp comparison and pair-level reads, not an individual Good/Better/Best state, and Stone did not build one from a stat line. The injury is a medical status, not an effort or toughness finding.
Alan Ball.established: He won and held the outside job on camp evidence; pair-level coverage reads and teams portability add context. No specific individual technique fault is recorded, and injury is not effort evidence.
Alan Ball.staff_view: A long outside corner who can handle a defined starting coverage job and communicate exchanges. I see a balanced profile, with less playmaking and route anticipation than the better corners.

trait_findings.Communication: Taught angles and coverage/substitution exchanges held on spring retests; communication with Trawick transferred through camp. Spring angle work was not live tackling. A full live tackling/coverage profile and individual game responsibilities remain unrecorded.

strengths: Taught angles and coverage/substitution exchanges held on spring retests; communication with Trawick transferred through camp.
Retention. Each correction the spring record gives him (the tackling angle, the substitution call, the exchange call) is recorded as held at the next test. That is what the program asks of a rookie.
He earned a job nobody gave him: "no depth position set" in May, "without an established starting award" in camp, then the starting job beside Lowery, held all season.
Special-teams communication: with Trawick the clearest multi-unit communicator in camp, and the coverage-lane work in the preseason.
The goal-line interception, as a rep to keep once Oden's tape shows it came from the right spot in the call.
limitations: Spring angle work was not live tackling. A full live tackling/coverage profile and individual game responsibilities remain unrecorded.

Tackling angle. The one individual technique item on record, corrected in non-live work in May; the record holds no individual live tackling evaluation of him since. "Tackling is part of the scheme," so Oden's cutup sorts his 2013 tackle attempts by angle and leverage.

The weekly help rule and the unit items above, classified before any of it is assigned to him. Teaching state: Good at rookie minicamp is his only recorded state. The later records describe corrections retained and communication against changed pictures, which is how the framework describes Better, but no record assigns that state and Stone did not assign it after the fact.
Bacarri Rambo.established: Basic alignment/coverage and spring correction retention are supported; controlled pursuit-angle work improved. His rookie starting experience broadens the questions, not proof of complete live tackling or help mastery.
Bacarri Rambo.staff_view: A developing safety with useful ball instincts and improving exchange communication. I see the reads and communication becoming usable, while live tackling and play-action discipline need a firmer foundation.

trait_findings.Communication: Camp identified the cleanest, most stabilizing safety communication in the group. Interceptions are outcomes without a classified responsibility/catch-point sequence. No individual game technique flaw is assigned by the record.

strengths: Camp identified the cleanest, most stabilizing safety communication in the group.

Communication, the one individual practice evaluation the record holds: the cleanest and "most stabilizing" safety communicator in camp, before he and Rambo took first safety work at the August 3 staff review.
Available for all 18 games.

The takeaways the held-up lists kept: London, Cleveland and the Week 16 interception that became a touchdown two plays later. Oden's tape decides whether each came from the right spot in the call; if it did, it is a rep to keep.
limitations: Interceptions are outcomes without a classified responsibility/catch-point sequence. No individual game technique flaw is assigned by the record.

None the record assigns to him. The pass-defense and run-fit corrections in the table are unit items, each classified (assignment, communication, technique, physical loss, processing, coaching or teaching) before any of it is his. Where a help directive asked for two things at once, the first question is whether it said which came first; Stone said the directives were his.
Teaching state: the record holds camp communication reads, not a Good/Better/Best state, and Stone did not build one from a tackle total.
Dwight Lowery.established: Camp identified stabilizing safety communication. His request for clear help priorities exposes a shared-rule question, not proof of a coverage defect or an elite grade from interceptions.
Dwight Lowery.staff_view: A stabilizing safety whose communication, positioning and combination recognition support the coverage structure. I see anticipation and clean operation compensating for ordinary recovery movement.

trait_findings.Zone / pattern match: Coverage communication and leverage corrections held across changed spring distributions and inside/outside camp exposures; he identified a footwork error himself. Recovery after lost leverage and sustained outside coverage remain open. Nickel selection is not proof of a fixed ceiling or measured recovery speed.

strengths: Coverage communication and leverage corrections held across changed spring distributions and inside/outside camp exposures; he identified a footwork error himself.

Coverage communication and leverage, retained across every phase from rookie minicamp to camp. On those items the spring and camp record meets the framework's Better description: corrections retained and the job executed through changing looks (a changed receiver distribution in OTAs, a retest at minicamp, outside and inside positions in camp). That is a teaching state for those phases, not a label.
Self-correction: he found his own footwork fault in May.

He held the nickel job as a rookie, with no recorded change through the Divisional game, and dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both playoff games, with takeaways in Weeks 1 and 11 and the Divisional sack.
limitations: Recovery after lost leverage and sustained outside coverage remain open. Nickel selection is not proof of a fixed ceiling or measured recovery speed.
The draft board's objection is still open: recovery when a route beats his leverage. The season record neither answers it nor shows a failure; the tape has to.
The outside evaluation. Camp said it would continue; the weekly records carry him only at nickel, and no record closes it.
His reps inside the Week 17 and Wild Card corrections are classified before anything is assigned to him. No in-season teaching state is recorded.
Jordan Poyer.established: Communication, leverage and self-correction were retained across rookie camp, OTAs and camp, including inside/outside presentations. Nickel experience is real; recovery after lost leverage and the parked outside evaluation remain unresolved.
Jordan Poyer.staff_view: A developing nickel corner who can sort routes and maintain leverage through communication. I see short-area recognition ahead of outside recovery speed, press power and catch-point size.

strengths: He held the first outside-starting opportunity after Ball’s injury and retained that role through the postseason.

He took an outside job mid-season on a week's preparation and kept it. "Harris in Ball's spot" held up in his first start; when Bouye was cleared, Stone kept Harris in the job on the evidence then, and he started through both playoff games.
Available every week: dressed for all 16 regular-season games and both playoff games.
limitations: Selection alone is not a coverage technique grade. Individual target responsibility and isolated coverage are unrecorded; planned help does not prove inability.

Houston away first. The losses in his starts are written to the unit; his reps in Week 12, Week 14 and the Buffalo, Tennessee, Indianapolis and Wild Card corrections are classified by the state/05 categories before anything is assigned to him.
What the help plan asked of him. Weeks 11 and 12 were built around not leaving him alone and no later directive names him; the record does not say why, so Stone read it as a finding neither way.

Camp placed him in "the next band"; that is a comparison, not a finding. No record names a technique fault of his. Teaching state: the record holds no individual phase evidence for him, so Stone gave none.
Mike Harris.established: He stepped into outside work after Ball's injury. Help directives changed around him, while the record lacks an individual technique finding. That experience is useful without turning protected usage into a fixed ceiling.
Mike Harris.staff_view: A replacement starter or reserve corner who can execute a bounded outside role. I see usable movement without a defining press, ball or catch-point advantage.

trait_findings.Press coverage: Rookie alignment was correct and camp established a defined coverage-lane job with first outside-reserve exposure. A physical press-release loss occurred with the assignment intact; later press retests are absent. Random return credits do not establish specialist ability.

strengths: Rookie alignment was correct and camp established a defined coverage-lane job with first outside-reserve exposure.
limitations: A physical press-release loss occurred with the assignment intact; later press retests are absent. Random return credits do not establish specialist ability.
A.J. Bouye.established: Basic corner alignment was learned; one rookie-minicamp loss kept the assignment intact but lost physically at release. Coverage-lane work earned a teams role and he later served as outside reserve.
A.J. Bouye.staff_view: A developmental outside corner with enough movement and catch-point size to pursue a reserve role. I see press technique and route recognition behind the physical outline of the player.

strengths: The record establishes late-season first outside-reserve availability while Bouye was hurt.
limitations: No named spring/camp rep or individual technical correction is recorded. Return attribution and reserve status cannot rank coverage ability.
Kevin Rutland.established: The recorded outside-reserve workload began after injuries elsewhere; individual technique evidence remains thin. Return credits are unreliable, and no dated retirement has been established.
Kevin Rutland.staff_view: An outside-corner reserve with functional movement but an unfinished technique and recognition profile. I see a narrow depth role rather than a matchup I would consistently isolate.

strengths: Camp/preseason documented retention of the assigned coverage-unit lane job.
limitations: Defensive snaps and individual safety technique are absent. Lowery/Rambo’s cleaner communication comparison does not supply a full Prosinski grade.
Chris Prosinski.established: Camp prepared him for safety rotation; coverage lanes held in preseason. Lowery/Rambo separated in communication, but regular-season defensive opportunity is unrecorded.
Chris Prosinski.staff_view: A coverage-unit safety with useful straight-line range and a reserve defensive role. I see movement and lane work ahead of route-combination recognition and man coverage.

trait_findings.Communication: Multi-unit communication required decreasing coach rescue across OTAs, minicamp and camp. Defensive transition and individual safety coverage remain ungraded. Coverage-unit communication cannot substitute for a complete safety evaluation.

strengths: Multi-unit communication required decreasing coach rescue across OTAs, minicamp and camp.
limitations: Defensive transition and individual safety coverage remain ungraded. Coverage-unit communication cannot substitute for a complete safety evaluation.
Brynden Trawick.established: Previously taught special-teams jobs operated with less rescue through spring and strong multi-unit communication in camp. Defensive transition technique remains a baseline question, not a diagnosed flaw.
Brynden Trawick.staff_view: A physical developmental safety whose coverage-unit communication and run-support tools offer a path to playing time. I see his defensive recognition and coverage positioning as less developed.

strengths: Practice-squad membership is established; no individual football strength is documented.
limitations: No named individual rep, role-specific defensive evaluation or season statistic exists. The provisional CB trait set does not establish his exact defensive role.
Brandon King.established: There is no recorded individual defensive or teams evaluation from the practice-squad year. His request for a teams assessment is a real follow-up, not evidence that he lacks value there.
Brandon King.staff_view: A provisional corner/special-teams depth player who needs a clearly defined defensive job. My view is that movement and support utility offer more than a developed coverage specialty.

strengths: The branch establishes a safety practice-squad role; earlier experience is background only.
limitations: No named 2013 rep or individual safety evaluation is recorded. His real-world CB classification is separate and cannot overwrite the branch role.
Antwon Blake.established: Earlier NFL participation is part of his background; this staff's 2013 individual record is absent. Moving to the practice squad is not a measured regression.
Antwon Blake.staff_view: A small, mobile developmental defensive back being reviewed at safety in this branch. I see quickness and pursuit utility ahead of the route reads and positioning required for a full safety role.

strengths: The season records sustained punting exposure; unit operation was described as clean through the first half.

Operation. Every recorded read of the specialist operation, from the spring through Week 8, is clean. From Week 10 no operation read was kept, so Stone called the rest of the season unread, not clean.
Available for every game.

The Week 2 held-up line, the Wild Card fair catch at the 13, the Divisional punt downed at the 9 and the late Divisional punt after which Tennessee started at its own 10 are noted, not claimed: without the special-teams film review Stone could not separate them from the spot and the coverage.
limitations: Catch-to-kick time, hang and direction are not measured. Sampled punt outcomes, return responsibility and the Week 12 zero-distance entry do not classify his skill.

Plus-territory punting. Lowry's own rematch note named "plus-territory punt execution" after the punt downed at the line from the Houston 49. That punt is the one the record names; its cause (snap, protection, contact or kick) is not recorded, and Stone did not name one.

Punt and coverage on the three returns that went on correction lists: Martin 26 (Week 12), Martin 33 (Week 14, after "better punt lanes" was the plan) and Hilton 26 on the last snap at Indianapolis. Each is classified as punt (hang and placement against the intended punt), coverage (lane and leverage) or call.
Teaching state: none is recorded for him; the records speak to the unit, and Stone did not build one from the averages.
Bryan Anger.established: Spring/camp and early-season specialist operation were recorded as clean. Later punt outcomes lack a complete split between instruction, kick and coverage; gross average is insufficient.
Bryan Anger.staff_view: A strong-legged punter whose best weapon is gross distance. I see hang and operation as useful, with directional and plus-territory control less developed than the leg.

strengths: The record includes a strong bye-week practice make result and perfect recorded kicking from Week 14 through the Divisional game.

The kicks that tied games or won them went in: the Week 3 tying kick with 5:41 left and the winner on the final snap, the third-quarter 47 that tied Week 5, the Week 13 overtime winner, and the Week 14 extra point that put Jacksonville ahead with 3:34 left.
The finish. He made every field goal and extra point he attempted from Week 14 through the Divisional, including five field goals in Week 17.
The first half of the season: 14 of 15 at the bye, with the weekly record showing no operation issue in any of those games.
limitations: The midseason short/long misses and missed try have no kick/snap/hold cause. The old flat long-distance model cannot grade leg range or pressure consistency.

Apart from the 51 at Denver, the misses clustered from Week 10 to Week 13: 22 and 27 at Tennessee, 30 against Arizona, 48 and an extra point at Cleveland. All five went on the weekly correction lists, the Tennessee pair as "Two missed field goals inside 30 yards." None is classified by cause. Stone told him he would not call any of them a kick problem, a snap, a hold or protection until the special-teams review says which, and told him the Week 10 to 13 tape had not been broken down that way.
Teaching state: the record gives none for a kicker, and Stone did not build one from make totals.
Josh Scobee.established: Clean early specialist operation provides a baseline; the late-season miss cluster and subsequent makes are review locators, not a diagnosis of technique or mentality.
Josh Scobee.staff_view: A starting NFL kicker with a useful long-distance leg and dependable established operation. I see range and ordinary accuracy ahead of precision kickoff control and my confidence in repeated pressure consistency.

strengths: Unit operation was reported clean through the first half with full-season long-snapper availability.
limitations: No snap-specific accuracy, velocity, trajectory or timing measurements are recorded. Later operation is unassessed; kicking misses cannot be assigned to him.
Jeremy Cain.established: Recorded spring/camp and Weeks 1–8 operation was clean. Later snaps lack their own assessment because the engine recorded no snapper credit; missing statistics are not missing contribution.
Jeremy Cain.staff_view: A specialist long snapper whose primary value is repeatable delivery and routine operation. I see snap utility as stronger than protection transition or coverage athleticism.
